item: ROADMAP §5 item 13 (M6), area J: a species-tree null for the grammar by comparison
registered_in_its_own_commit: Written after the code was frozen in a commit and before any J reading was computed under either null. The run reads each reading once, against this file.
question: Two of area J's readings count agreement of orthologue presence species by species. Which of them survive a null in which the agreement comes from shared ancestry alone?

A_library_pairs.section: GRAMMAR-BY-COMPARISON §14 (2026-09-12), with §11's headline pairs through their §14 rows
quotes: **What is more alike than age predicts.** 35 of 860 pairs at a false discovery rate of 5%, led by the immune and signalling libraries: immune against the ligand-receptor protocol (observed −0.76, age-matched −0.93, z 9.3), degradation and cytoskeleton against the same protocol (z 8.5), the cell cycle against immunity (z 6.7), blood with the growth-longevity axis (observed +0.72 against −0.27).

**Both headline findings of §11 are age.** Random age-matched sets already correlate at 0.55 to 0.73 where the developmental libraries sit, so axes with segmentation reads z 1.9, heart with musculoskeletal 2.2, germ layers with the nervous system 1.6, none significant. The cores against the ligand-receptor protocol match their null (replication −0.87 against −0.79, z −0.9).
A_library_pairs.why_the_tree_changes_it: §14's null holds age and not the tree: a random age-matched set's profile is close to its age class's average, so the null's spread is small, while a library's own departure from its age expectation is one trait evolving along the tree and agrees across a clade because the clade shares an ancestor. A z of 9.3 against that spread counts each of 355 species as an observation.

quotes: | clear of the null (0 draws at or above) | **21** | | marginal (1–9 draws above) | 7 | | **at or below the null (≥10 draws above)** | **14** |

**The ones that survive are patchy and lineage-restricted**: `timer.developmental_timing` (+0.0413), `systems.extracellular_matrix_adhesion` (+0.0393), `blueprint.segmentation` and `timer.segmentation_clock` (+0.0381 each).

Even the matched-gene null draws genes independently of the tree, so a clade-wide loss counts once in the library and once in each draw but the *correlation structure* between the drawn genes is whatever the genome supplies rather than what a model of the tree would say. Felsenstein contrasts or a birth-death model along a species tree is what would settle a pair, and this project holds no tree.
B_library_coherence.why_the_tree_changes_it: §19's matched genes are matched on prevalence, not on where on the tree a gene was born: two genes born in the same clade share every absence outside it by descent, and a library whose members share a birth clade co-occurs more than prevalence-matched genes of mixed births without any loss in common.

readings_not_retested.\u00a710 origin per gene and age per lib: a placement (the deepest clade with an orthologue), not agreement between profiles; shared ancestry is what it reads, so a null of shared ancestry does not apply. The tree's birth nodes are reported beside the strata for the record only.
readings_not_retested.\u00a711 residual correlations on full m: §14 already re-read them on exclusive members against age; they are re-tested through their §14 rows (named_rows_reported_individually).
readings_not_retested.\u00a714 pairs far less alike than age (: recorded and not called by §14; the test stays one-sided, more alike.
readings_not_retested.\u00a719 null one, the prevalence shuffl: §19 itself rejects it as measuring non-independence.
readings_not_retested.gene pairs: §19 called no gene pair a dependency, and 188 million gene pairs are a separate test with its own multiple-testing design; not attempted here.
readings_not_retested.\u00a712, \u00a713 and \u00a715 to \u00a: one locus across species, families and composition, and the enhancer, assay and sequence readings: none counts agreement of presence across species.

tree.why_these: Ensembl Compara's own species trees, the trees its protein trees were built on, so the tree is the one the orthologue calls of the presence matrix already assume; release 63 of Ensembl Genomes is the pan-taxonomic counterpart of Ensembl 116, the release of both homology dumps the presence matrix was streamed from
tree.merge: the vertebrate tree's Vertebrata (the common ancestor of human and sea lamprey) replaces the pan tree's vertebrate clade; Ciona intestinalis, an outgroup only the vertebrate tree carries, is placed as sister to Ciona savignyi, as the vertebrate tree places it; any other conflict raises
tree.species_matching: production name, then without the assembly suffix, then the RENAMES table (12 renamed taxa), then a unique tip extending the name or the genus and species; two candidates or two species on one tip raise

branch_lengths.registered: Grafen (1989), rho 1: a node's height is its number of descendant tips minus one, the root's scaled to 1. Neither file has lengths both halves share (the pan tree has none), so a length is a modelling choice; Grafen's is the conventional one for a topology
branch_lengths.sensitivity: every branch length 1; reported beside the registered reading and deciding nothing

A.statistic: §14's own: Pearson r over the 355 species between two libraries' residual profiles (share of the members exclusive to each side with an orthologue in the species, minus the share of all 19,391 genes), r_exclusive, recomputed and required to match the stored value
A.model: each side's profile P = E + D, with E the age expectation (the exact mean profile of §14's own matched draw: per origin stratum, the members' count times the mean profile of every gene of that stratum, over the members with an origin) and D the deviation. Under the null E is held and D is replaced by an independent Brownian motion along the species tree, D ~ N(mu, sigma^2 C), with C the tree's covariance (shared root-to-ancestor length) and sigma^2 the REML estimate from D itself, (D - mu_GLS)' C^-1 (D - mu_GLS) / (n - 1); mu is irrelevant to r. The two sides' motions are independent; the statistic is recomputed on E + D_sim for each draw

parameters.p: (number of draws with r at or above the observed + 1) / (draws + 1), one-sided, more alike
parameters.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg over every testable pair, q at or below 0.05, as §14 did; the draws are shared across pairs (two banks), which keeps each p exact and makes different pairs' p values dependent

calibration.what: one random pair of gene sets per testable pair, each set drawn to its side's origin-stratum make-up (§14's own draw), tested exactly as a library pair
calibration.ceiling: more than 10% of them at p at or below 0.05 and the null is not calibrated: no reading

power.what: each library split at random into two halves, tested as a pair: the halves share the library's history, so a null that never sees them as alike cannot see a pair
power.floor: fewer than 50% of libraries at p at or below 0.05 and a result with no survivor is read as low power

A.falsifier: §14's reading that a pair is more alike than age predicts is re-read as age plus shared ancestry for every one of its 35 pairs whose q under this null is above 0.05, provided the null is calibrated; if none of the 860 survives, the 35 are what age and shared ancestry give on this model
A.descriptive_only: the GLS (phylogenetically whitened) correlation of the two deviations, the null's mean and sd, and the equal-length run; none decides

decision_rule.1_reproduce: if the testable pairs are not §14's (same pairs, same count) or any pair's recomputed r_exclusive differs from the stored one by more than 0.0001, select not_reproduced
decision_rule.2_calibration: else if more than 10% of the calibration pairs (one random pair of gene sets per testable pair, each set drawn to its side's origin-stratum make-up) have p_tree at or below 0.05, select null_not_calibrated
decision_rule.3_none: else if no library pair has q_tree at or below 0.05: select none_survive_low_power when fewer than half of the libraries' random halves have p_tree at or below 0.05, otherwise none_survive
decision_rule.ties: 'at or below' includes equality; 'more than 10%' and 'fewer than half' are strict
decision_rule.always: the equal-length sensitivity sentence is appended to whichever outcome is selected, except not_reproduced, and decides nothing

outcome_wordings.not_reproduced: No reading: §14's observed statistic did not reproduce. {n_mismatch} of {n_tested} testable library pairs differ from the stored r_exclusive by more than 0.0001, or the testable pairs are not §14's {n_tested_14}, so the pairs this null would judge are not the pairs §14 judged.
outcome_wordings.null_not_calibrated: No reading: the species-tree null is not calibrated on this data. Of {n_cal} pairs of random gene sets drawn to the tested pairs' origin-stratum make-up, {cal_hits} ({cal_share}) have a tree-null p at or below 0.05, above the registered ceiling of 10%, so the null finds random genes alike more often than it should and a library pair's p under it is not evidence. §14's {n_14} of {n_tested} pairs stand as written, with their caveat.
outcome_wordings.none_survive: None of the {n_tested} testable library pairs is more alike than age and shared ancestry predict: under a Brownian null along the Ensembl Compara species tree (Grafen branch lengths), no pair has a Benjamini-Hochberg q at or below 0.05, and that includes all {n_14} pairs §14 called more alike than age at the same false discovery rate. The null is calibrated ({cal_hits} of {n_cal} random age-matched pairs at p at or below 0.05) and sees {halves_hits} of {n_halves} libraries against their own random halves at p at or below 0.05. On this model the {n_14} pairs are what age and shared ancestry give, and no library pair is called a dependency.
outcome_wordings.none_survive_low_power: None of the {n_tested} testable library pairs is more alike than age and shared ancestry predict under a Brownian null along the Ensembl Compara species tree (Grafen branch lengths): no pair has a Benjamini-Hochberg q at or below 0.05, including the {n_14} pairs §14 called more alike than age. This is weak evidence against them: the null is calibrated ({cal_hits} of {n_cal} random age-matched pairs at p at or below 0.05) but sees only {halves_hits} of {n_halves} libraries against their own random halves at p at or below 0.05, below the registered half, so on this tree the test has little power and a pair's failure does not show that it is inertia. No library pair is called a dependency.
outcome_wordings.some_survive: {n_surv} of {n_tested} testable library pairs are more alike than age and shared ancestry predict under a Brownian null along the Ensembl Compara species tree (Grafen branch lengths; Benjamini-Hochberg q at or below 0.05): {k_14} of the {n_14} pairs §14 called more alike than age, and {k_new} that §14 did not call. The other {lost_14} of §14's {n_14} do not survive the tree. The null is calibrated ({cal_hits} of {n_cal} random age-matched pairs at p at or below 0.05) and sees {halves_hits} of {n_halves} libraries against their own random halves at p at or below 0.05. The surviving pairs meet, on this model and these branch lengths, the condition the area set before a pair could be called a dependency; agreement of presence along the tree does not show that one library acts on the other, and an orthologue's presence is not function.

A.sensitivity_wording: Under equal branch lengths instead of Grafen's, {n_surv_eq} of {n_tested} pairs have q at or below 0.05, {k_14_eq} of them among §14's {n_14}, and {cal_hits_eq} of {n_cal} random age-matched pairs have p at or below 0.05; the registered reading is the Grafen one.

B.statistic: §19's per-library mean Jaccard over all member pairs of their presence sets (exact over every pair, where §19 sampled 60,000 pairs for the largest libraries), less the mean of the same over the model's draws of the members: the library's excess over its own tree model
B.model: stochastic Dollo along the species tree with human added: a gene is born at the common ancestor of human and the species carrying it and lost independently on the branches below, never on the path to human. A branch's loss probability p_e is (losses + 0.5) / (genes at risk + 1.0) from every gene's Dollo reconstruction (at risk: the gene is held at the branch's parent); a gene's survival on a branch is (1 - p_e)^theta_g, theta_g fitted by bisection so that its expected number of species equals its observed number
B.null: the same excess for random gene sets matched member for member on birth node, drawn without replacement per node; the model removes birth clade and loss rate, the real genes remove what the model misses for every gene alike
B.classes: clear: (k + 1) / (B_SETS + 1) at or below 0.05, k the random sets whose excess is at or above the library's; at_or_below: 2k at or above B_SETS; marginal otherwise. With 20 sets these are exactly §19's classes
B.falsifier: §19's reading that a library's members co-occur beyond prevalence-matched genes is re-read as birth clade and loss rate on the tree for every one of its 21 clear libraries that is not clear here
B.descriptive_only: the number of random sets whose observed mean Jaccard exceeds every model draw (how far the model misses real genes), and the libraries' excesses; none decides

decision_rule.1_reproduce: if any library's member count differs from §19's members_with_a_profile, or its exact mean pair Jaccard differs from §19's stored value by more than 0.005, or the libraries are not §19's 42, select not_reproduced
decision_rule.2_none: else if no library is clear, select none_clear
decision_rule.3_chance: else if the number of clear libraries is at or below chance_ceiling(n_lib) (the smallest k with binomial(n_lib, 0.05) CDF at or above 0.95), select at_chance
decision_rule.classes: clear: (k + 1) / (B_SETS + 1) at or below 0.05, k the random sets whose excess over their own tree model is at or above the library's; at_or_below: 2k at or above B_SETS; marginal otherwise

outcome_wordings.not_reproduced: No reading: §19's observed statistic did not reproduce. {n_mismatch} of {n_lib} libraries differ from §19's member count or from its mean pair Jaccard by more than 0.005, so the libraries this null would judge are not the libraries §19 judged.
outcome_wordings.none_clear: No library's members co-occur beyond what the species tree and real genes predict. Each library's mean pair Jaccard, less what a stochastic Dollo model of every member's own birth and losses along the Ensembl Compara species tree predicts, was set against the same quantity for {n_sets} random gene sets matched member for member on birth node: 0 of {n_lib} libraries are clear (empirical one-sided p at or below 0.05), {n_marg} are marginal and {n_below} sit at or below the random sets' median. None of the {n_19} libraries §19 called clear of prevalence-matched genes stays clear. On this null their coherence is what birth on the tree and loss rate give; nothing is called a dependency.
outcome_wordings.at_chance: {n_clear} of {n_lib} libraries' members co-occur beyond what the species tree and real genes predict, which is no more than chance gives. Each library's mean pair Jaccard, less what a stochastic Dollo model of every member's own birth and losses along the Ensembl Compara species tree predicts, was set against the same quantity for {n_sets} random gene sets matched member for member on birth node: {n_clear} are clear (empirical one-sided p at or below 0.05), {n_marg} marginal and {n_below} at or below the random sets' median. With no effect anywhere about {expected_chance} of {n_lib} would be clear, and {ceiling} or fewer 95 times in 100 if the libraries were independent. {k_19} of the {n_19} libraries §19 called clear are among the {n_clear}. No library's coherence is read as beyond the tree; nothing is called a dependency.
outcome_wordings.some_clear: {n_clear} of {n_lib} libraries' members co-occur beyond what the species tree and real genes predict. Each library's mean pair Jaccard, less what a stochastic Dollo model of every member's own birth and losses along the Ensembl Compara species tree predicts, was set against the same quantity for {n_sets} random gene sets matched member for member on birth node: {n_clear} are clear (empirical one-sided p at or below 0.05), {n_marg} marginal and {n_below} at or below the random sets' median; with no effect anywhere about {expected_chance} would be clear, and more than {ceiling} would arise by chance at most 5 times in 100 if the libraries were independent. {k_19} of the {n_19} libraries §19 called clear stay clear, and {k_new} that §19 did not call clear are clear here. This is agreement of presence across species beyond birth clade and loss rate; it names no pair, calls nothing a dependency, and an orthologue's presence is not function.

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record e06b1ca

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
